QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron in the first Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom if the velocity of an electron in the first orbit is $2.2 \times 10^6$ m/s. [mass of electron = $9.1 \times 10^{-31}$ kg, Planck's constant $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J·s]

Solution.S:
The de Broglie wavelength is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$.

Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J·s, $m = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}$ kg, $v = 2.2 \times 10^6$ m/s.

$$\lambda = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 2.2 \times 10^6}$$

$$= \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{2.002 \times 10^{-24}} = 3.31 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{3.31 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}}$$

Hence, the correct option is A.
